sub_rqs.question: How do morpheme-aware tokenization methods, including hybrid morphological analysis plus subword approaches, compare with purely statistical subword tokenizers on Korean downstream NLP task performance?
sub_rqs.rationale: This is the central question of the topic: whether linguistically informed segmentation improves task performance over standard subword methods.
queries: Korean morphological analysis BPE hybrid tokenizer
Korean pre-trained language model morphological segmentation

sub_rqs.question: How do standard subword algorithms (BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece unigram, byte-level) behave on Korean agglutinative morphology and Hangul script, and what modifications to them have been proposed?
sub_rqs.rationale: This establishes the baseline behavior and the limitations of existing subword methods, and identifies concrete modification strategies.

sub_rqs.question: How do vocabulary design choices (vocabulary size, composition, multilingual vs. monolingual vocabularies) affect Korean token efficiency, sequence length and model performance?
sub_rqs.rationale: The dependent variables include vocabulary efficiency, and vocabulary design determines the trade-off between compression and quality.
queries: vocabulary size effect Korean language model
token count sequence length Korean text efficiency

sub_rqs.question: What intrinsic metrics and evaluation protocols are used to assess Korean tokenization quality, and how well do they correlate with downstream performance?
sub_rqs.rationale: Determining whether a method is improved requires valid measures of tokenization quality beyond end-task scores.
queries: intrinsic evaluation tokenization quality morphological alignment

sub_rqs.question: How are tokenization improvements for Korean adapted in large language models, including tokenizer replacement or vocabulary extension in pre-trained models and the effects on cost and generation quality?
sub_rqs.rationale: Current Korean LLM practice involves adapting the tokenizer of existing models, which raises questions about transfer, inference cost and performance.
queries: Korean large language model tokenizer adaptation
language model tokenizer inference cost Korean

sub_rqs.question: What robustness issues and unintended effects do Korean tokenizers exhibit, such as handling of spacing errors, noisy user-generated text, out-of-vocabulary words, and rare morphological forms?
sub_rqs.rationale: Improvements may fail on noisy or non-standard text, so risks and conditions of use need to be understood.

search_strategy: Search 2016–present, with emphasis on 2019 onward, covering the transformer and LLM era, using OpenAlex and arXiv, and ACL Anthology-type venues surfaced through them. Prefer empirical studies with comparative baselines on Korean benchmarks (e.g., KLUE, NSMC, KorQuAD) and tokenization analyses; exclude papers that are only about Chinese or Japanese segmentation unless they offer transferable methods for agglutinative languages. I expect rq4 (intrinsic evaluation of Korean tokenization) and rq6 (robustness) to be the thinnest in the literature.}
